manager_rule: After computing stub candidates for any round in which compiler_kelvin_omission fires (per Rule 33): enforce a per-net stub count cap of 1 for every net N that satisfies ALL of the following — (i) N is not a /SENSEC{M}_HI or /SENSEC{M}_LO Kelvin net, (ii) N is not a USB or CAN differential-pair net, (iii) N does not appear in failing_reasons with 'has unconnected ratlines'. If the compiler has generated more than 1 stub candidate for such a net N in the current round, retain only the single highest-priority stub for N and discard the remainder BEFORE the absorber stage. Log 'per_net_stub_cap_applied' with fields: (a) round number, (b) each net N where the cap fired with original stub count and discarded count, (c) total stubs freed by the cap, (d) confirmation that freed stub slots are available for Rule-33 force-injected Kelvin stubs. Rationale: when compiler_kelvin_omission is active the compiler is exclusively generating multi-stub proposals for non-failing nets (observed at round 71: 7 stubs / 3 nets = 2.33 stubs/net, all absorbed), consuming all stub capacity and delivering zero routing guidance to FR for the failing Kelvin region. Capping at 1 stub per non-critical net during omission rounds structurally prevents this capacity leak without requiring absorption threshold history. This rule is additive to Rules 33, 34, and 37 and does not replace or defer any action those rules independently mandate.
